Target Symbols appear on player names in meetings and mid-game, usually only visible to the role they pertain to and/or the dead. • Executioner targets are marked with [color=#643B1F]X[/color] • Inquisitor heretics are marked with [color=#D94291]$[/color] to the dead. • Fairy targets are marked with [color=#B3FFFF]★[/color]

Protection Symbols appear on player names in meetings and/or mid-game, showing that they are immune to most attacks. These are usually only visible to the role they pertain to, their target, and/or the dead. • Medic shields are marked with [color=#006600]+[/color] • Cleric barriers are marked with [color=#00FFB3]Ω[/color] • Warden fortification is marked with [color=#9900FF]π[/color] • Mirrorcaster's reflections are marked with[color=#90A2C3]〚〛[/color] • Fairy Protection is marked with [color=#FFD900]★[/color] • Guardian Angel Protection is marked with [color=#66AAF3]☀[/color] • Oracle blessing is marked with [color=#BF00BF]†[/color]

Status Effects appear on player names in meetings and mid-game, usually only visible to the role they pertain to and/or the dead. • Arsonist douses are marked with [color=#FF4D00]Δ[/color] • Plaguebearer plague is marked with [color=#E6FFB3]¥[/color] • Controlled players are marked with [color=#FF2660]⦿[/color] • Blackmailed targets are marked with [color=#2A1119]M[/color] • Hypnosis is marked with [color=#D53F42]@[/color] • Spellslinger Hex is marked with [color=#FF0000]乂[/color] • Monarch Knights are marked with [color=#EA535B]♠[/color]

• [color=#8CFFFF]Investigative[/color] roles can gather information about other players. They can use this info to deduce who is crew or not. • [color=#8CFFFF]Killing[/color] roles can [color=#FF8B95]kill[/color] others, but [color=#FF8B95]killing[/color] [color=#8CFFFF]Crewmates[/color] may have consequences. • [color=#8CFFFF]Protective[/color] roles have a way to defend other players, sometimes themselves as well. • [color=#8CFFFF]Power[/color] roles usually influence votes or have stronger abilities compared to other [color=#8CFFFF]Crewmates[/color]. • [color=#8CFFFF]Support[/color] roles usually have ways to help the rest of the [color=#8CFFFF]Crewmates[/color], or may just benefit themselves.

• [color=#8A8A8A]Benign[/color] roles cannot win by themselves, either helping others or surviving as long as possible. • [color=#8A8A8A]Evil[/color] roles set out to complete their goals, staying as kingmakers, leaving in victory, or ending the game abruptly. • [color=#8A8A8A]Killing[/color] roles set out to be the last [color=#FF8B95]killer[/color] alive at all costs. • [color=#8A8A8A]Outlier[/color] roles set out to achieve their own goals, but each role impacts the game differently, sometimes behaving like a mix of [color=#8A8A8A]Benign[/color], [color=#8A8A8A]Evil[/color], and [color=#8A8A8A]Killing[/color] roles.

• [color=#FF0000]Concealing[/color] roles have the ability to [color=#FF8B95]kill[/color] as well as deceive others or hide away while doing so. • [color=#FF0000]Killing[/color] roles have enhanced or altered [color=#FF8B95]killing[/color] abilities, allowing them to [color=#FF8B95]kill[/color] more effectively. • [color=#FF0000]Power[/color] roles have abilities that can be deemed far stronger than any other roles, granting [color=#FF0000]Impostors[/color] a shift in strength. • [color=#FF0000]Support[/color] roles can help hide away bodies or to make [color=#FF8B95]killing[/color] more accessible.

Role List Buckets are only relevant when the "Set Role List" setting is used for role spawning. • Common [color=#8CFFFF]Crew[/color] contains Investigative, Protective, and Support roles. • Common [color=#FF0000]Impostor[/color] contains Concealing and Support roles. • Common [color=#8A8A8A]Neutral[/color] contains Benign and Evil roles. • Special [color=#8CFFFF]Crew[/color] contains Killing and Power roles. • Special [color=#FF0000]Impostor[/color] contains Killing and Power roles. • Special [color=#8A8A8A]Neutral[/color] contains Killing and Outlier roles. • Wildcard [color=#8A8A8A]Neutral[/color] contains Benign, Evil, and Outlier roles. • Non-[color=#FF0000]Impostor[/color] contains all [color=#8A8A8A]Neutral[/color] and [color=#8CFFFF]Crewmate[/color] roles. • Random buckets spawn any role of said faction (like Random [color=#8CFFFF]Crew[/color]). • The Any bucket allows any enabled role to spawn.

Common Slang is usually coined by the TOU and TOS communities to quickly pass information. • HC stands for Hard-Cleared, meaning a player is undoubtedly innocent. • Glorphing is a term used when someone is taking on the appearance of another player, whether that's from a [color=#00FF00]Glitch[/color], [color=#FF0000]Morphling[/color], [color=#FF0000]Shapeshifter[/color], or any other similar role. • Ghostwalkers are terms used to describe roles like [color=#D4D4D4]Haunter[/color] and [color=#662961]Spectre[/color], as a way to differentiate them from standard ghost roles. • Sidebars are called when a player is pulled aside in a Proximity Chat lobby to discuss private matters.
